story.headline: Duke-led team uses a 13-ion quantum simulator to watch particle 'strings' break and new pairs form
story.summary: A team led by the Duke Quantum Center used a trapped-ion quantum simulator to watch "string breaking", the process in which pulling two linked particles apart creates new particle pairs. The work was published in Nature Physics on September 23, 2026. The researchers encoded the model into a chain of 13 ions controlled by focused laser beams, and the university calls it one of the earliest demonstrations of its kind.

quote.text: Researchers led by the Duke Quantum Center (DQC) have used a quantum simulator to observe string breaking dynamics connected to particle antiparticle formation, marking one of the earliest demonstrations of its kind in quantum physics.
